items.title: US air force removes all bombers from British military base RAF Fairford
items.description: A statement says all bombers deployed to RAF Fairford have been "re-deployed to their home stations" in the US.

items.title: Brazil election goes to run-off as right-wing Flávio Bolsonaro wins first round
items.description: With neither candidate getting more than 50% of the vote, the election will go to a run-off on 25 October.

items.title: Watch: How Brazil's dramatic election unfolded
items.description: Millions of Brazilians took to the polls on Sunday for the first round of the country's presidential elections.

items.title: Trump unveils 'Super Intelligence Force' to oversee AI policy
items.description: The president named his national intelligence chief as the taskforce's head as worries over AI grow.

items.title: France closes up to 500 schools Monday over student protests
items.description: Lessons will be "totally or partly suspended" in some high schools after clashes between riot police and student protesters, France's education minister says.

items.title: All six passengers presumed dead after plane went missing off US coast
items.description: The aircraft lost communication with flight controllers after significantly dropping in altitude, according to flight data.

items.title: Supporters of jailed ex-PM Imran Khan march to Pakistan capital
items.description: Thousands have taken to the streets after talks between authorities and Khan's party ended in deadlock.

items.title: Kyiv bridge hit in further Russian drone attack as German chancellor makes surprise visit
items.description: Footage shows a drone hitting the Pivnichyi (Northern) Bridge as vehicles move across it, creating a large fireball.

items.title: Forced to call him 'Dad': Trial over sexual abuse in disabled care home shocks South Korea
items.description: The BBC spoke to one of three residents at a care home who were sexually assaulted by a staff member.

items.title: Yemen's government announces all-out war to reclaim land from Houthis
items.description: The Yemeni president's announcement comes amid an exchange of strikes between the Houthis and the Saudi-led coalition.

items.title: Ethiopian rebel forces withdraw from Tigray regional capital
items.description: Two residents in Mekelle tell the BBC pro-government forces have taken control of the city.

items.title: Watch: What we know about Russian strikes on Kyiv bridges
items.description: BBC Ukraine correspondent Dan Johnson is near Kyiv's Northern Bridge, which has been hit for the second day in a row.

items.title: Indian police accused of sexually harassing journalists at protest
items.description: The allegations were made after police detained dozens of protesters demanding the resignation of the election chief over changes to voter rolls.

items.title: Christa Pike's prognosis still unclear after failed execution, lawyer says
items.description: Pike's lawyer says doctors are still trying to clear two lethal doses of pentobarbital from her body.

items.title: Why Canada is wargaming a (long shot) US invasion
items.description: Prime Minister Mark Carney has said the military is running scenarios in the unlikely case the US invades Canada.

items.title: Why pastors may not be seen - or heard - preaching on Ghana's buses for much longer
items.description: Ghana is a predominantly Christian country where preaching on public transport is widespread.

items.title: Could El Niño mean there are no Atlantic hurricanes this year?
items.description: For the first time in three decades there has not been a single Atlantic hurricane in September, normally the most active month.

items.title: Rare tornado whips through small Australian town
items.description: The twister was caught on camera in Ulladulla, New South Wales, damaging property and downing trees.

items.title: Why has Brazil accused the US of election interference?
items.description: The Latin American country will vote for its next president, as Lula da Silva and Bolsonaro clash over sovereignty, security and ties with Washington.

items.title: Will Spain's housing crisis lead to a snap election?
items.description: The BBC's Guy Hedgecoe is in Madrid, where a series of marches have been scheduled, after Spain's Congress rejected measures aimed at tackling the country's housing crisis.
